issues.detail: The Greek 'ο λογος ημων' (our word) refers to the word/message of the speakers, but the Vietnamese 'lời chúng tôi nói' adds the verb 'nói' (speak/say) which is not explicitly in the Greek. More importantly, the Vietnamese 'chẳng phải vừa "phải" vừa "không"' (not both 'must' and 'not') is a significant mistranslation of 'ουκ εγενετο ναι και ου' (was neither yes nor no). The Greek describes a state of being/existence (e.g., 'it was not yes nor no'), whereas the Vietnamese interprets it as an obligation or a choice between 'must' and 'not'.
